findings.proof_contract: The response lists database-registered routes that appear nowhere in source
findings.description: Routes are registered from the route_config table, so the HTTP surface is data. No source file names /legacy/reports or /legacy/ledger; they exist only because a row says so, and GET /api/routes discloses the full set including the SQL each runs.

findings.proof_contract: A route served only by the module named in PLUGIN_PATH responds
findings.description: require(process.env.PLUGIN_PATH) loads a module chosen by the environment with no allowlist. Whoever controls PLUGIN_PATH controls which code the application executes, and the loaded plugin's routes are served to any caller.

findings.proof_contract: The response contains a row whose author column holds an admin username
findings.description: The beta exporter ships behind FEATURE_BETA_EXPORT and never went through review, so it still concatenates the account parameter into SQL. A UNION across to users returns every role including admin.

findings.proof_contract: A subscription is created for an attacker-controlled URL, and the follow-up delivery is accepted with no signature and no authentication
findings.description: When WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true the application exposes subscription registration and an unauthenticated, signature-free delivery endpoint. Anything that finds the surface can register a destination and push forged events straight into the audit log.

findings.proof_contract: The tautology returns every user row, including admin
findings.description: The executed SQL text is read out of query_config and run, with the request's filter value interpolated into it. Two independent problems: the statement can be rewritten without a deploy, and the parameter is never bound.

findings.proof_contract: The response contains the live environment including the JWT signing secret
findings.description: if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') app.get('/api/debug', ...) registers a diagnostics route that returns the whole process environment, including JWT_SECRET and DATABASE_URL. It exists only in the deployment that matters most.

findings.proof_contract: The injected command's output appears in the response
findings.description: The plugin loader requires every file in the plugin directory on boot, and nothing imports src/plugins/audit.ts. The endpoint it adds concatenates the cmd parameter into a shell string, so discovering the plugin system leads straight to command injection.
